conflicts.proposed_title: Add: tauri-plugin-updater self-update — install/restart commands, signed latest.json in release, cask auto_updates
conflicts.resolution: Coexist. KEN-394 (Mac app is ad-hoc signed; Gatekeeper reports it damaged) is Apple code-signing; the updater's minisign keypair is independent. But a macOS self-update that swaps an ad-hoc-signed .app can re-trigger the Gatekeeper 'damaged' state — the U3 release smoke checklist must exercise the macOS relaunch path with KEN-394 still open, and resolving KEN-394 remains the real fix.

conflicts.proposed_title: Add: strict shared update-feed schema in core; CLI ported with downgrade refusal
conflicts.resolution: Coexist. KEN-395 (no Intel-mac or linux-arm64 builds — install channels error on those machines) means feed.json and the signed latest.json will not carry assets for every platform; the schema and updater flow must degrade to 'View release notes' on a platform with no matching asset rather than erroring, until KEN-395 adds those builds.

project_placement.project_description: Sidebar update notice with per-install-method actions, signed self-update, and the account surface across app and kendex.ai — implements docs/plans/update-notice-and-account.md (GPT 5.6 Sol adversarial review folded in).
project_placement.rationale: One project, not two. The parts are independent except the sidebar-bottom slot, but they share one reviewed plan document, the slot's layout lands exactly once (the account row issue depends on the notice-store issue that creates it), and ~30 issues fits comfortably in a single project. Two projects would turn that single UI coupling into a cross-project relation for no tracking benefit. kendex-web issues stay in this same project on team KEN: the app-side account work consumes the web endpoints directly and the parity gate is shared contract fixtures in both repos, so splitting by repo would sever the dependency chain (aggregate API → web pages → devices → app client → app UI). No existing backlog project fits: all six are long-lived area projects (CLI & Distribution etc.), and this is a bounded product feature spanning app + web. No project-level relations: nothing here consumes or enables another project's output.
